title: POC playbook & hosting triage - Harborview Logistics
next_steps: Redwood to share pilot runbook + pricing sheet (Maya) by 2026-05-01
Customer to provide 2-week representative request traces and token distributions (Marcus) by 2026-04-30
Schedule initial benchmark window week of 2026-05-04 (Leo + Marcus)
Security questionnaire follow-up: send SOC2 + KMS integration notes (Rina) by 2026-05-03
action_items: Maya - send tailored pilot quote and SOW draft - due 2026-05-01
Leo - prepare benchmark harness and sample scripts (includes 1k, 5k, 20k concurrency profiles) - due 2026-05-04
Marcus - upload last 14 days of production request traces (anonymized) to shared drive - due 2026-04-30
Samir - list compliance requirements (data residency, KMS/HSM, audit window) - due 2026-05-03
summary: Discovery / POC scoping to decide between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for an inference pilot. Customer emphasized throughput (burst to 1.2k RPS), tail latency targets (<200ms for p50/p90), and data residency + KMS controls. Redwood AE/SE proposed a 6-week pilot with week 1-2: baseline benchmarks on hosted, week 3-4: dedicated sizing trial, week 5: security review, week 6: decision and rollout plan.
topics: Workload sizing: QPS, token distribution, concurrency
Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Security and compliance (KMS, SOC2, audit logs)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone thanks for joining, we have about 55 minutes, is this still a good time?
[00:04] Priya Shah: yes thanks, we wanted to lock down what success looks like for a pilot, also get clear on perf numbers we're going to run.
[00:12] Leo Alvarez: great, I'll cover the benchmark plan and the tradeoffs between hosted / dedicated / private. quick note: some transcription artifacts, sometimes KV cache comes out as KV cash in our notes.
[00:22] Jenna Ortiz: quick context, we power a realtime routing recommender across carriers, so typical requests are short (~50-100 tokens) but we do occasional long consolidation prompts ~800 tokens.
[00:35] Marcus Lee: infra constraints: we prefer not to egress sensitive manifests, everything must stay in our EU region and we need KMS-backed key control.
[00:44] Maya Chen: understood. quick qual - what's your current peak RPS and expected burst?
[00:50] Marcus Lee: steady is ~250 rps, bursts up to 1200 rps for surge windows, concurrency spikes are short but frequent during load balancer failover tests.
[01:05] Leo Alvarez: ok that's helpful. target latency? p50 / p90 boundaries?
[01:09] Jenna Ortiz: product asks for sub-200ms p50 and p90 under normal load; p99 is less critical but should be reasonable.
[01:17] Maya Chen: great, put differently: we need low tail latency for small prompts and predictable TCO. now i'll run through the proposed 6-week pilot.
[01:29] Priya Shah: timeline sounds good, can you outline what we do each week?
[01:33] Maya Chen: week 0 - kickoff and access, week 1-2 - hosted baseline benchmarks using our curated small model family and a medium model, measure latency and throughput, week 3 - dedicated sizing trial with reserved capacity to test autoscaling and burst response, week 4 - private (if required) feasibility for VPC/on-prem constraints and KMS validation, week 5 - security deep dive, week 6 - decision and roll-out playbook.
[01:55] Marcus Lee: we may skip private if hosted + dedicated meets KMS + residency needs, but we need to verify KMS integration with our HSM.
[02:05] Rina Patel: on the KMS front, Redwood's private deployments can integrate with customer-managed KMS; hosted supports envelope encryption + BYOK patterns but needs certification for some HSMs. we'll bring documentation.
[02:18] Samir Dutta: for compliance, SOC2 plus a 90-day audit log retention is a must. can you support longer retention for dedicated/private?
[02:28] Leo Alvarez: yes, retention windows are configurable for Dedicated and Private; hosted has standard retention but we can add enterprise retention as an add-on.
[02:36] Jenna Ortiz: how do fallbacks work if a model or capacity tier fails during bursts? we don't want routing to add 100s ms.
[02:44] Leo Alvarez: we recommend policy-based smart routing - priority route to dedicated pool then fallback to hosted compatible variant. in practice we do model variant fallbacks (quantized smaller variant) which keeps latency stable.
[02:57] Priya Shah: cost sensitivity is high. can you give a rough cost delta for similar throughput across modes?
[03:03] Maya Chen: rough heuristics: hosted gives fastest time-to-value but higher unit cost at sustained throughput; Dedicated reduces per-token costs at scale (commitments), Private has highest fixed cost and operational overhead but best control. we'll send a sample cost comparison aligned to your 250 steady / 1.2k burst profile.
[03:23] Marcus Lee: for dedicated, how fast is burst scaling? our concern is cold-start for GPU pools.
[03:29] Leo Alvarez: dedicated pools can be configured with warm capacity for instant bursts; autoscaling has a few minutes to spin up extra nodes if not warmed. warm pools (keep-n instances) avoid cold start for critical routes.
[03:40] Jenna Ortiz: benchmark specifics - we need to see p50/p90/p99 across three payload sizes: small (50t), medium (300t), long (800t).
[03:49] Leo Alvarez: agreed. we'll run 3 concurrency buckets: steady low (250 concurrent), medium (700 concurrent), burst (1.2k concurrent). also test different sequence lengths to exercise KV cache and batching.
[04:03] Priya Shah: what about model variants? we use a fine-tuned open model with 8k context. will Redwood host fine-tuned weights?
[04:11] Rina Patel: yes, we support customer model artifacts; we recommend creating a pinned version in the catalog for benchmarking. there are quantization options, but we should validate quality drop for aggressive quant.
[04:24] Samir Dutta: security checklist: VPC peering, private link, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, signed attestations. Redwood, can you meet all these for a pilot?
[04:36] Maya Chen: yes for Dedicated and Private modes we can support VPC peering and private connectivity; hosted supports PrivateLink in some regions. SAML SSO and RBAC are standard. we'll send the security pack.
[04:48] Marcus Lee: data residency - we need EU-only processing and storage. hosted regions available in eu-west, correct?
[04:54] Maya Chen: correct, eu-west and europe-west-2 are available; we'll confirm region endpoints and data processing agreements in the SOW.
[05:03] Jenna Ortiz: success criteria - list out measurable pass/fail for pilot so execs can greenlight next step.
[05:09] Leo Alvarez: proposed success criteria: 1) p50 < 150ms and p90 < 250ms for small/medium workloads under steady load; 2) sustained throughput of 250 rps with ability to handle 1.2k burst with warm-pool fallback; 3) cost per 1M tokens under dedicated pilot comes within target 30% of current cost model; 4) KMS integration validated and SOC2 docs provided.
[05:34] Priya Shah: product also needs qualitative checks - response fidelity within current fine-tuning tolerances. we will run an eval set.
[05:42] Rina Patel: sure, we'll run regression evals against your gold set and flag quality regressions >2% F1 drop.
[05:49] Marcus Lee: benchmark mechanics - how do you collect traces and define representative traffic?
[05:54] Leo Alvarez: we provide a harness that can replay traces (anonymized) with token-level timing; we also stress with synthetic bursts. need to confirm tokenization matches your tokenizer to avoid mismatch in token counts.
[06:08] Jenna Ortiz: timeline again - when can we start?
[06:12] Maya Chen: if we get traces by 2026-04-30 we can start hosted baseline week of 2026-05-04, dedicated sizing week of 2026-05-11, security deep dive week of 2026-05-25, decision/rollout by 2026-05-31.
[06:27] Priya Shah: sounds good. any blockers on Redwood side?
[06:31] Rina Patel: nothing major; need clarity on HSM vendor for KMS validation and agreement on data residency in SOW.
[06:39] Samir Dutta: also would like to run a 4-hour sustained burst test to see thermal throttling and cost burn rate.
[06:46] Leo Alvarez: we can schedule an extended burn window as part of the dedicated sizing trial. note: sustained 4-hour bursts are expensive but useful for thermal profiling.
[06:57] Jenna Ortiz: how do we measure cost in pilot to make apples-to-apples comparison? token metrics alone miss infra overhead.
[07:03] Maya Chen: agreed - we'll produce per-token unit cost + infra amortized cost per hour + warm-pool reservation costs. deliver a cost-per-1M tokens with sensitivity to burst frequency.
[07:18] Marcus Lee: what about monitoring - do we get per-model dashboards?
[07:22] Leo Alvarez: yes, per-route metrics, token-level breakdowns, per-token latency histograms, and tracing hooks. we can wire your Datadog or Grafana via metrics export.
[07:33] Priya Shah: any regulatory review for private deployment on prem? expected timeline?
[07:38] Rina Patel: on-prem/private gets extra legal/ops time - typically 8-12 weeks for full private packaging and audit; pilot feasibility can be validated faster but production private cutover is longer.
[07:50] Maya Chen: that's why we recommended hosted->dedicated first; if it meets KMS/residency we can avoid the long private track.
[07:57] Jenna Ortiz: fine. can you send a short one-pager that maps our workload to recommended mode?
[08:01] Maya Chen: yes. action: we'll craft a hosting decision rubric: inputs (QPS, burst profile, residency, KMS, latency target, cost sensitivity) and output (recommended: hosted/dedicated/private) with confidence levels.
[08:13] Priya Shah: last question - are there any pitfalls you commonly see?
[08:16] Leo Alvarez: common issues: underestimating long-tail requests, not warming pools, quantization regressions impacting quality, and forgetting network egress costs in cross-region fallbacks.
[08:28] Marcus Lee: note taken. thanks.
[08:30] Maya Chen: great thank you all. we'll share the pilot runbook, pricing, and security pack. schedule the benchmark for week of May 4th. any final comments?
[08:40] Jenna Ortiz: none from me.
[08:42] Priya Shah: no thanks.
[08:43] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll follow up. meeting adjourned.
